setting: A student is meeting with a career counselor about finding a summer internship.
narrator_intro: Listen to a conversation between a student and a career counselor.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: I've applied to about fifteen marketing internships so far and haven't heard back from any of them. I'm starting to think my resume is the problem.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Let's take a look. Actually, your experience is solid, but the resume is formatted more like an academic CV than a professional one. It's a bit dense for recruiters who skim quickly.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: I didn't realize that mattered so much. What should I change?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Cut it down to one page, use bullet points instead of paragraphs, and lead each bullet with an action verb. Also, move your marketing club experience above your part-time retail job, it's more relevant.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: That makes sense. Should I also mention the class project where we developed a mock ad campaign?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Definitely, that's exactly the kind of concrete experience recruiters look for. Quantify it if you can, mention any metrics from the project, even estimated ones.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Okay, I'll revise it tonight. Is there someone here who can review it before I resend applications?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Yes, drop it off at the front desk once it's revised, and we'll have feedback back to you within two business days.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.

questions.correctAnswer: Improving a resume to get more responses from employers

questions.correctAnswer: It resembles an academic CV rather than a professional resume
